behaviour: ;V,<name>,<int|true|false|TOGGLE|INC[,n]|DEC[,n]> sets a volatile variable and ;VP the persistent one (verb any case, the comma after V/VP required, non-numeric literals read 0, INC/DEC default 1); malformed forms print their usage/needs-a-value line and create nothing.
gap: The lower-case command letter (';v,' and ';vp,' / ';Vp,') is dispatched at WCB.ino:8044 and the p at :247 but no test sends it.
how: Send ;v,hilv,5 and ;vp,hilp,6 then ?VAR,GET each; expect the values and [persistent] for hilp in ?VAR,LIST.

behaviour: A name is 1-15 characters of letters, digits and underscore, case-sensitive; anything else is refused with the Invalid name line.

'all' in any case is refused as a name by ;V, ;VP and ?VAR,SET; ?VAR,CLEAR,ALL wipes the table (persistent ones included), removes the NVS blob key so the clear works on a full store, and nothing loads at the next boot.
gap: The legacy branch that clears a variable literally named 'all' (:370-372) cannot be reached: nothing can create one any more. The clear-on-a-full-NVS case (the remove needs no space) is not run on a full store.

behaviour: Out-of-range literals saturate at INT32 (toInt); INC past INT32_MAX wraps (characterised, undefined behaviour).

;VP persists (NVS blob wcb_vars) and survives a reboot; ;V on an existing persistent variable keeps it persistent (never demotes); ;VP promotes a volatile one; an unchanged set skips the NVS write; only persistent variables reach ?backup.
gap: The skipped NVS write on an unchanged set (:172-179) is not observable from the console (flash wear only).

behaviour: The ;V/;VP set confirmation '[VAR] <name> = <v>  [persistent|volatile]' prints only under ?DEBUG,ON, even when unchanged; ?VAR,SET always prints its '[persistent]' ACK.
The table holds 100 variables: a new one past the cap recycles the lowest-slot volatile variable silently; with 100 persistent ones ;VP and ?VAR,SET print 'table full' and create nothing.

A persistent set or clear NVS refuses prints '[VAR] ERROR: NVS write failed (see ?NVS)', prints no '[persistent]' ACK, puts RAM back to what the next boot loads (a created variable removed, an edited one restored) and a refused ?VAR,CLEAR keeps the variable; a reboot holds exactly what was acknowledged.
gap: the edit of an existing persistent variable on the full store added 2026-10-12: refused, old value back in RAM and after the reboot (run 20261012-135536). The could-not-open-NVS line stays unasserted (needs a fault knob). Remaining: the [VAR] ERROR: could not open NVS line (:99), which needs a fault knob.
how: On the full store (seq.nvs_full_consistency's fill) ?VAR,SET an EXISTING persistent variable to a new value: expect the ERROR line, ?VAR,GET still the old value, and the old value after a reboot.

behaviour: At boot the wcb_vars blob is parsed into persistent variables (a line with an invalid name is skipped) and '[VAR] Loaded N variable(s)' prints only when N > 0.
gap: The skip of an invalid name inside the blob (:133) needs a crafted blob: no command writes one.

behaviour: ?VAR / ?VAR,LIST print the table with the N/100 footer; ?VAR,SET,<name>,<int|true|false> (absolute only: TOGGLE/INC read 0), GET, CLEAR,<name|ALL>; verbs prefix-match (SETUP, GETX, CLEARX); the usage and 'Unknown' lines.
A ?VAR line ending in '?' prints help and does not execute; ?VAR? prints the VAR section.
?backup and the config pull emit each persistent variable as ?VAR,SET,<name>,<v> after the device lines and before ?ETM, in both chains, never a volatile one.

;M!<name>=<v> (any case of M) stores a RAM-only variable only for names m1..m8*, never overwrites a persistent variable, prints only under ?DEBUG,MAESTRO; from a mesh client the same name limit applies while its ;V/;VP are unrestricted.
Variables are per board: ;W2,;V and ;W2,;M! set W2 only, a ;V typed on W1 never reaches W2, a mesh client's broadcast ;V sets every WCB, and a ;VP sent over the mesh survives the target's reboot.

IF,<var><op><int> with = != < > <= >= and negative literals; an unset variable reads 0; IF creates nothing; the right side is an integer literal only ('true' reads 0, '==' is '=' against 0); lowercase 'if' and spaces work.

AND/OR in any case, evaluated strictly left to right with no precedence; misplaced/trailing AND|OR, two conditions without an operator, an empty or no condition each print a '[VAR] IF: <reason>' line and fail closed; a malformed term OR'd with a true one still fails closed.

A false IF skips exactly the next actionable token: comments (***) do not use up the gate, consecutive IFs AND together ('[IF] skipped (earlier condition false)'), a bare ;T under a false IF is dropped and gating continues, ';T<n>,cmd' is dropped and uses up the gate, a true IF keeps delays.
An IF in a timer chain is decided when the chain is parsed (changing the variable during the delay does not cancel); a set-and-test in one chain normally reads the old value (characterised).

IF as a ;T payload or inside a ;W payload is rejected with its own error and the next command runs ungated; an IF before a ;W route gates the whole route; an IF gates a whole ?SEQ,SAVE token including a value that holds ^ or ;T.
An IF run on W2 through ?MGMT,FRAG tests W2's variables; an IF inside a stored sequence is saved verbatim and evaluated at each recall.

Sequences are the lines '<key>,<value>' of one LittleFS file on the spiffs partition, in save order: ?NVS counts them, a save grows the file by key+value+2, an in-place edit keeps the name's place, a re-save of the same value writes nothing, a clear gives it all back, none of it touches NVS; the store holds 32768 bytes.

A save that would take the file past SEQ_FILE_MAX is refused with 'the sequence store is full - see ?NVS' and leaves nothing listed or in ?backup; every stored one is in ?backup with whole CRC-valid chains; a clear on the full store works and makes room.
A value over SEQ_VALUE_MAX (3999) is refused with 'Failed to store sequence <k> (it is N characters - the limit is 3999). Not stored.'.
gap: No test reaches the TOOBIG refusal: inv.seqget_largest's ladder tops at 2950 and W1 in AP mode runs out of heap copying a 4 KB line first (its refusal is the OOM line).
how: With W2's WiFi off (more heap) push a 4000-character ?SEQ,SAVE to W2 through ?MGMT,FRAG (23 chunks) or type it on W2's USB; expect the 'limit is 3999' line, ?SEQ,NAMES unchanged and ?SEQ,GET NOTFOUND. Skip when the OOM line prints instead.

behaviour: A key is 1-15 characters (16 refused by ?SEQ,SAVE and ?CS, change nothing); key_list and seq_mig_done are reserved everywhere (save, clear, recall, GET answers NOTFOUND, NAMES hides them); a clear by a 16-character key leaves the 15-character key's sequence.
gap: A key holding a comma or a line break (SEQ_E_BADVAL, :863-865) cannot be typed: the comma ends the key and a line reader ends the line.

behaviour: seqStoreBegin at boot: a partition with no file system is formatted ('Setting up the sequence store (first use)...'), an unreadable one is started over with its sequences lost, a crash while mounting last boot or ?DEBUG,SEQNVS puts this boot on the NVS fallback (its sequences in the file unseen), no spiffs partition / out of memory / a store that will not open fall back too, a file with no seq_mig_done marker (NVS blanked) is cleared, NVS sequences are moved in, and '[SEQ] N stored sequence(s) in the sequence store (x of 32768 bytes)' prints.
gap: Asserted: the SEQNVS fallback line and the move. Not asserted: the first-use format line, the 'could not be read - starting it over' line, the crash-while-mounting guard (RTC word), the no-marker clear (an NVS blanked under a live file: only an esptool NVS erase does that), and the '[SEQ] N stored sequence(s)' count line on an ordinary boot (boot.banner_w1/w2 do not check it).
how: In boot.banner_w1/w2 add the '[SEQ] N stored sequence(s) in the sequence store (' line with N = the chain's ?SEQ,SAVE count. The first-use and starting-over branches need a knob that formats the partition (opt-in: it loses the sequences) or an attended fresh board.

behaviour: Sequences a fallback boot (or older firmware) saved in NVS move into the file at the next boot: a key both hold takes NVS's value in its own place, a new one goes last, each is read back before NVS lets go, the key list keeps what did not move, and the move line says how many; a phantom listed with no value is dropped, a value over 3999 or with a line break or one that does not fit the file stays in NVS with its own line.
gap: The phantom drop ('was listed with no sequence stored under it'), the 'cannot move into the sequence store' (over 3999 / line break), the 'does not fit in the sequence store', the 'did not read back' count and the rewrite-failure line are not asserted.
how: On the SEQNVS fallback with NVS full (seq.nvs_full_consistency's fill) a ?SEQ,CLEAR that answers SEQ_E_LIST leaves the name listed with no value; reboot and expect the '[SEQ] <k> was listed with no sequence stored under it: dropped from the list.' line and the key absent from ?SEQ,NAMES. The does-not-fit arm: fill the file to its 32 KB, then on a fallback boot save one more and reboot: expect its 'does not fit' line and NVS still listing it.

behaviour: The inventory hash is FNV-1a over the key list 'k1,k2,...,' then each value, each followed by a 0xFF separator (an empty store hashes to 7A0B824E); cached, invalidated on every write, recomputed lazily; equals the WDP SEQHASH advert and ?MGMT,SEQ.
gap: The 5 s retry after a hash failure (:879-887, a store that will not mount) is not reachable without a fault knob.

behaviour: On the NVS fallback (stored_cmds namespace) a save that fails leaves no phantom (the value is taken back out when the list cannot grow), a clear removes the value before the list rewrite, a clear whose list rewrite fails says the name is still listed empty (SEQ_E_LIST), and nvsClear re-stamps seq_mig_done so the legacy migration never re-imports.
gap: The SEQ_E_LIST clear outcome ('Removed the value of <k>, but NVS could not update the sequence list') is not asserted: seq.nvs_full_consistency expects the clear on the full store to say 'Deleted'.
how: On the full NVS fallback clear the newest key: either 'Deleted' or the SEQ_E_LIST line is acceptable, but then ?SEQ,NAMES must still list it and ?SEQ,GET must answer NOTFOUND/empty, and a second clear after freeing room must remove it.

behaviour: A damaged record (no comma, empty or over-long key, no final newline) is skipped and counted by every walk, ?NVS says 'damaged lines skipped', a rewrite drops it, and an append after a file not ending in a newline starts a new line first.
gap: No command can write a damaged line (LittleFS commits at close, a failed write leaves the file as it was).
how: A RAM-only ?DEBUG knob that appends a raw damaged line to /seqs (as PULLFAULT does for config lines); then ?NVS must say 'damaged lines skipped', ?SEQ,NAMES must hide it, and a save must drop it.

behaviour: ?NVS ends with the store line 'Sequences: N in the sequence store, x of 32768 bytes (partition spiffs: u of t bytes used)' with READ ERROR / damaged suffixes, or on the fallback 'Sequences: kept in the settings store this boot (<why>)'.
gap: Only the 'Sequences: N in the sequence store, x of y bytes' head is matched (STORE_RX); the partition-usage tail and the fallback line's exact text ('kept in the settings store this boot (?DEBUG,SEQNVS asked for it ...)') are not asserted (the fallback test only checks the head is absent).
how: In seq.store_accounting match the whole line including '(partition spiffs: u of t bytes used)' with u <= t; in seq.store_moves_from_nvs assert the fallback ?NVS line and its SEQNVS reason.

behaviour: ?SEQ,SAVE,<key>,<value> (verb any case, letter function identifier too) stores and confirms 'Stored: Key=..., Value=...'; the value ends only at '^?' ('^;' and '^text' stay, a trailing '?' is kept, not the help trap); 'Invalid format' / 'Key or value cannot be empty'; an out-of-memory copy names its cause; a save invalidates the hash so WDP re-advertises.

?SEQ,GET,<key> prints '[MGMT:SEQVAL,<n>]<key>,OK|NOTFOUND,<value>' (case-sensitive keys, usage line); ?SEQ,NAMES prints '[MGMT:SEQ,<n>]<hash>,<count>,<names>' in save order; ?SEQ,LIST prints the header, rows in save order and the footer, or 'No stored commands.'; an unknown sub-command prints 'Invalid SEQ command. Use: ?SEQ ?'.
gap: The 'Could not read the sequence store right now - try again.' NAMES answer and the '(its value could not be read)' LIST row need a store fault.

behaviour: ?SEQ,CLEAR,<key> deletes ('Deleted stored command key'), a missing key says 'No stored value found ... but removed from list if present', an empty name is refused; ?SEQ,CLEAR,ALL and legacy ?CCLEAR wipe every sequence ('All stored sequences cleared') and re-stamp seq_mig_done; ?CCLEAR,ALL no longer reaches a legacy setter.

;C<key> / ;c and ;SEQ<key> in any case recall a sequence, with ,L / ,LOCAL / ,l for local-only; the empty-key forms print their usage, a wrong-case or missing key says 'No command stored under key', a 16-character key is refused before the fan-out, a reserved name is refused, 'Recalling command for key' echoes the body.
gap: 'Could not read sequence <k> (<why>) - not run.' (:653-656) needs a store fault.

behaviour: Recall strips *** comments from each ^-part before running; a comment-only sequence says 'Sequence contained only comments — nothing to execute.'.

A top-level ;C/;SEQ recall typed locally broadcasts one normalised trigger (;C<key> or ;SEQ<key>, never ',L') before the local run; ,L, a mesh-received trigger and a nested recall in a body stay local; a body's commands run with local origin so plain text in it still broadcasts.

A sequence already on the item's lineage (direct or ring self-recall, case-sensitive hash) is refused after one expansion; nesting stops at 8; a sub-sequence reused in one run expands every time (back-to-back, across ;t, at two depths); the board keeps answering.

A nested expansion that would leave fewer than 16 command-queue slots free is refused whole with one 'nearly full' line; a top-level body longer than the free queue is refused whole ('has N commands and the command queue has room for M') and runs nothing; no per-token 'queue is full' lines.

A recalled body that holds ;T runs through the timer engine (its delays kept) unless it carries a value verb (?SEQ,SAVE/?CS/?MGMT), which goes through the chain walker; a recalled timer chain replaces a running one.

Legacy ?CS<key>,<value> saves (keeping ^ chains, ending only at '^?'), two ?CS on one line split, ?CE<key> erases, either case; a ?C-first line with a trailing ^?CHK (or ^<lfi>CHK, lower case, zero-stripped) is verified on its own, bounded at the next delimiter, and only the text the checksum covers runs.
?config's 'Stored Sequences:' section lists '  <key> = <value>' per sequence or '  None', and names a store that could not be read.

migrateOldStoredCommands recovers CMD1..CMD80 from the legacy stored_commands namespace and orphaned stored_cmds keys once, normalises ^*** markers, stamps seq_mig_done and prints the [MIGRATION] summary at every boot without the marker.
gap: No command writes the legacy keys; only the 'No legacy sequences found' line on the boot after an erase is reachable, and nvs.erase_* do not assert it.
how: Assert '[MIGRATION] No legacy sequences found — nothing to recover.' on the erased board's first boot in nvs.erase_defaults_restore; the recovery itself needs a legacy image or a raw-NVS write knob.

behaviour: ?MGMT,SEQ,<n> / ?MGMT,SEQGET,<n>,<key> relay the inventory and one value over the mesh with per-requester dedup, TOOBIG past 2903 characters, and the argument errors.

?HW,<n> and legacy ?HW<n> save 1/21/23/24/31/32 to NVS (hw_version), update the running value at once (the chain reports it), refuse an unknown value before writing and refuse the other chip family's versions; the pin map applies only at boot.

At boot loadHWversion reads hw_version (0 when unset: 'SET YOUR HARDWARE VERSION BEFORE PROCEEDING!!', 'No LED was setup', every port on GPIO5), ignores a version saved for the other chip with '[HW] Saved HW version N is for the other chip - ignored', and applies the pin map; the banner prints 'HW Version: x.y'.
gap: The other-chip-ignored boot line cannot be reached (the setter refuses it) except from older firmware's NVS; the pin maps for 2.1, 2.3, 3.1 and 3.2 have never run (known: WCB-WP59 pinmap.unverified_revisions); printHWversion's duplicated 31 branch (:177-180) is cosmetic.
how: The reachable part is covered; the rest needs an S3/2.x board on the bench or a raw-NVS knob writing hw_version=32 on a classic board.

behaviour: ?LED prints 'LED pin: GPIOn' and the usage; ?LED,PIN,<0-48> saves led_config, re-inits the NeoPixel on the new pin and confirms; a pin outside 0-48 is refused; the boot prints 'LED pin override from NVS: GPIOn' and applies it; ?ERASE,NVS removes it; ?backup emits LED,PIN only on HW 3.1/3.2.
gap: the refusals and the boot-time ignore of a refused saved pin added in 99b14e8/fc1407d; run 20261012-212755. Still attended: a visibly moved LED
how: Unattended half: ?LED,PIN,<own pin> then a reboot asserting 'LED pin override from NVS: GPIO<n>' (what _led_override does) without the erase; the abc case once the firmware validates digits.

behaviour: updateBaudRate accepts ports 1-5 and the 13-rate table, refuses a soft port (S3-S5) above 115200, warns above 57600, applies live, updates the RAM table and NVS, and warns when NVS refused it (the port still runs the rate, ?config shows the running rate).

?LABEL,Sx,<text> saves serial_labels (30 characters max), a refused NVS write keeps the old label and prints no 'set to' line, a removal needs no space; labels load at boot and show in the port rows and the chain.

?ALIAS saves wcb_config/alias trimmed, with ^ , ; ? CR LF replaced by '_', cut to 24 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary, cleared with ?ALIAS,CLEAR; loaded at boot ('Loaded WCB alias: <a>'), emitted in the chain, resolved by peers after a reboot.

?WCB,<n> (1-20, legacy ?WCB<n>) saves wcb_config/WCB_Number, takes effect live for the number and at boot for the radio address, peers and ETM; a sender id that is not its MAC's last octet is dropped by receivers meanwhile.
?WCBQ,<n> (1-20, legacy ?WCBQ<n>) saves wcb_quantity, reconciles peer registrations live, is loaded at boot and counted in the banner and ?config.
?WCBCH,<1-11> saves mesh_channel for the next boot (0 and 12 refused), the boot applies it with esp_wifi_set_channel, and an out-of-range NVS value falls back to the default.
gap: The corrupt-NVS fallback (:535) and the 'esp_wifi_set_channel FAILED' boot line (channels 12-13) are unreachable through the setter (known: WCB-WP59 row 14 channel clamp).

behaviour: ?EPASS,<1-39 chars> (and legacy ?EPASS<pw>) saves espnow_config/password and the live password every packet carries; argument errors; the boot loads and prints it.
?DELIM / ?FUNCCHAR / ?CMDCHAR (and legacy ?D<x>, ?LF<x>, ?CC<x>) save command_config and load at boot; the banner and ?config show them; collisions and bad characters refused.
?CONTROLLER,ON,<id>/OFF save wcb_config special_peer and special_peer_id (1-20); the boot registers the special peer only when enabled; a custom id outlives a disable in the chain.
?MAC,2|3,<hh> (two hex digits, legacy ?M2xx/?M3xx) saves mac_config and changes the receive filter at once; the radio address and the peer table use the octets at boot.

?BCAST,OUT/IN flags save bdcst_set / bcast_block (S0 echo included), load at boot, warn when NVS refused them ('they revert at the next reboot'); ?RESET_BROADCAST / ?BCAST,RESET rebuild the namespace with every port open and S0 off.
gap: The full-NVS warning lines for the output and input flags (:394-395, :1991-1992) are only used as a Skip condition, never asserted.
how: On the full NVS fallback (nvs_fill) send ?BCAST,OUT,S4,OFF: expect the port silent to a broadcast now, the warning line, and the flag back ON after a reboot.

behaviour: Serial mappings save serial_map with _act last, free the keys of cleared slots and outputs past the count, warn when the count could not be stored and never load a half-written slot.
loadSerialMonitorSettings reads the serial_monitor namespace (mon1-5, mirror flags) that nothing writes; saveSerialMonitorSettings has no caller.
gap: Dead: the 'Serial Monitoring' section can only read None.

behaviour: Maestro slots (maestro_cfg), Kyber mode/port (kyber_settings) and Kyber targets (kyber_targets) load at boot; a legacy remote-to-self Maestro slot is repaired into a local slot and saved ('[MAESTRO] repaired legacy remote-to-self slot').
ETM settings save etm_config and load at boot with defaults (MISS 5, TIMEOUT 500, BOOT 2, HB 10, COUNT 20, DELAY 100, CHKSM on); out-of-range stored values are healed at load.
gap: The heal of an out-of-range stored value (:2763-2766) is unreachable through the range-checked setters (known: WCB-WP59 row 14 ETM range heal).

behaviour: The learned-peer mask is saved to learned_peers 5 s after a change with the MAC octets it was saved under, flushed again just before a deferred restart, frozen by ?ERASE,NVS; at boot a table saved under other octets is discarded, else each peer is registered and '[PEER] restored N learned peer(s) from NVS' prints.
WiFi mode, AP SSID/pass and JOIN SSID/pass save to wifi_cfg and load at boot before wcbWifiStart; a mode byte above JOIN reads as OFF.
gap: The corrupt-mode clamp (:57) needs a raw-NVS write.

behaviour: ?NVS prints the usage line (used/free/available/total/namespaces/%) and one line per namespace, alphabetical, with entry counts that add up, then the sequence-store line and 'End of NVS'.

?ERASE,NVS and legacy ?WCB_ERASE clear the sequence store, every named namespace and then every namespace in the partition (WiFi, learned peers, saved devices, led_config included), freeze the learned-peer flush, clear PWM mappings without an inline restart, print the erased count and the ?HW reminder, and defer the restart so a chained command still runs; the board then boots on firmware defaults; a bad argument prints the usage and erases nothing.

?backup / ?BACKUP / WCB_WEBTOOL_CONFIG_PULL print the header, a warning when no HW version is set, one line per command, the configured chain (live delimiter and identifier, DELIM/FUNCCHAR/PEERSLIVE left out) and the factory chain ('^' and '?', identifier flipping after ?FUNCCHAR), each with a CRC-32 of exactly the bytes printed, in one write per line; a line that could not be built is left out and warned about after each output; chains near 6 KB print whole.
gap: The 128-byte stack fallback when the 2 KB writer cannot be malloc'd (:7842-7843) is a known-blocked fault path (WCB-WP59 fault.oom_and_init_failures).

behaviour: collectConfigCommands emits, in order: HW, LED,PIN (HW 3.x only), MAC,2/3, WCB, ALIAS (if set), WCBQ, WCBCH, WIFI (AP/JOIN with passphrase, or OFF), PEERSLIVE (factory chain only), EPASS, DELIM/FUNCCHAR (factory only, non-default), CMDCHAR, the Kyber release (KYBER,CLEAR or MAESTRO,REMOTE), BAUD x5, LABELs, BCAST OUT S1-S5+S0, BCAST IN, MAP,SERIAL lines, Maestro/MP3/DFP/HCR/WLED/VAR sub-emitters, KYBER,LOCAL (after the Maestros), ETM x8, CONTROLLER (ON,<id> or ON,<id>+OFF for a custom id), WDP,OFF / WDP,AUTOJOIN,OFF only when off, SEQ,SAVE per sequence, MAP,PWM,OUT and MAP,PWM last.
gap: Asserted: HW first, PEERSLIVE factory-only, CONTROLLER forms, VAR before ETM, WDP OFF tokens present, replay idempotent. Not asserted as an order: the Kyber release before the BAUD lines and KYBER,LOCAL after the Maestro lines (the restore-ordering rule), SEQ,SAVE after the ETM/WDP block, MAP,PWM last, WIFI,OFF emitted when off (only checked after an erase), LED,PIN on HW 3.x (needs an S3 board).
how: A read-only test over W1's and W2's chains: assert the token-family order above (index of ?KYBER,CLEAR|?MAESTRO,REMOTE < first ?BAUD; ?KYBER,LOCAL after the last ?MAESTRO; every ?SEQ,SAVE after ?ETM,CHKSM; ?MAP,PWM tokens last; a ?WIFI token present in every chain).

behaviour: A chain whose last token is ^<lfi>CHK<crc> (or ^?CHK, lower case, zero-stripped) is verified with CRC-32 of the text before it ('Command checksum VERIFIED - Configuration is intact') and then split and run; a mismatch prints FAILED/Aborting and runs nothing; an earlier ^?CHK inside the chain is a token; a 250-token chain past the 200-slot queue runs every token; the configured chain on a '!' board and the factory chain on a '?' board each verify as one line.

W1's own chain replayed one line at a time is accepted line by line and leaves the chain unchanged; after an erase, ?HW + a boot + every line + a boot + ?WDP,ADD of the learned peers put the board back exactly.
verifyBackupChecksum ('Checksum verification command received') has no dispatcher: a bare ?CHK<crc> line is an unknown command.
gap: Dead code.

behaviour: ?config / ?CONFIG prints the identity block, the port rows (RAM tables, not a re-read of NVS), Broadcast Blocking, Serial Monitoring (always None), the ESP-NOW block (password, MACs, peers with Online/last seen/Not yet seen, the controller row), the mappings, the command settings, Stored Sequences, the ETM settings and the Kyber/Maestro block.
gap: Not asserted: the 'Broadcast Blocking:' section (a blocked port with its label), the 'Controller Peer: ENABLED (ID n)' line, the Peers 'Online (last seen Ns ago)' row for W2, and the Mirror lines (dead, known WP59 row 14).
how: Read-only: with ?BCAST,IN,S5,OFF set (persist.bcast_flags_reboot) assert '    Serial5 input blocked' under 'Broadcast Blocking:'; assert the Controller Peer line against the chain's ?CONTROLLER token and a 'WCB2: ... Online (last seen' row while W2 is up.

behaviour: setup() loads WCB_Number first, then HW, LED pin, Maestro/MP3/DFP/HCR/WLED, variables, WDP, Kyber, PWM, prints the reset reason and bootloader, repairs Maestro self-slots, loads alias, WCBQ, mesh channel, WiFi, controller, MAC; inits the LED; creates the command queue; prints the banner; opens the sequence store and the migration; loads bauds, labels, monitor, broadcast flags and mappings; begins the ports (PWM/Kyber reservations respected); sets up WiFi/STA/channel/MAC/EPASS; starts the AP or JOIN before esp_now_init; registers peers, the special peer, learned peers and the broadcast peer; loads the command characters and ETM; starts the tasks; disarms the boot guard. The banner matches the chain line by line.
gap: Fault branches (ESP-NOW init failure, command-queue creation failure, 'Failed to add peer', esp_wifi_set_channel failure) are known-blocked (WCB-WP59 fault.oom_and_init_failures).

behaviour: A one-shot 10 s esp_timer armed first in setup() and disarmed at its end restarts a board whose setup() hangs; a normal boot reaches the end of setup() in under 7 s and bumps the RTC boot-attempt counter by exactly one per ?reboot.
The boot guard firing (a hung setup() restarted by the esp_timer task) and a failed esp_now_init leaving it armed.
gap: Needs a fault knob that stalls setup().

behaviour: printResetReason names the reset reason and the per-core RTC codes; the boot-attempt counter lives in RTC noinit RAM behind a magic word and restarts at 1 after true power loss, climbing across software/watchdog/panic resets ('<-- board retried/reset before this boot').
gap: Only the software-reset path is asserted; a power-on reset restarting the count at 1 ('Reset reason: 1 - Power-on Reset') needs a power cycle, and the panic/watchdog branches need a crash.
how: After a bench power cycle read the first boot's 'Boot attempts since power applied: 1' and 'Reset reason: 1 - Power-on Reset' from the session log; a watchdog branch needs a crash knob.

behaviour: printBootloaderInfo prints 'Bootloader: stock (<date>)' on a stock bootloader and 'Bootloader: CUSTOM short-WDT ...' on the S3 custom one.
gap: No WCB test asserts the line (s46 asserts NaviCore's); WCB-WP59 says the classic 'stock' half is testable today.

behaviour: A CPU-only restart's stale GPIO interrupt enables are cleared before the ISR service is installed and listed as '[BOOT] Cleared a stale GPIO interrupt left armed by the restart on GPIO ...'.

behaviour: WiFi.persistent(false) keeps the driver from rewriting nvs.net80211 on every WiFi.begin/softAP (a JOIN retrying every 5 s grew it 36 -> 95 entries).

behaviour: After esp_now_init the boot registers every floor peer but self ('Added ESP-NOW peer'), the special peer when enabled, the learned peers and the broadcast peer, seeds the active-peer set and prints the ESP-NOW block with the MAC and password.
With ETM on the boot schedules a random heartbeat inside ETM,BOOT and three boot announces from 1.5 s on, 1.2 s apart.

?reboot / ?REBOOT / <lfi>reboot and a pushed or mesh ?reboot set rebootPending ('Reboot queued - restarting once the command queue is quiet'); loop() restarts once the queue is empty and quiet for 4 s, or 20 s after the request ('Restart held off N s ...'), never while a config pull job is sending; exempt commands (an RTERM re-arm to the same relay, ?STATS,RPT) do not hold it; the learned-peer table is flushed first; 'Rebooting now...' or the PWM variant; no ETM command is ACKed from then on.
gap: Only the exact spellings 'reboot' and 'REBOOT' are matched (:7237): a mixed-case '?Reboot' is an unknown command and no test says so either way.
how: Send ?Reboot and assert 'Unknown command: Reboot' and no 'Reboot queued' within 6 s (or, if the product wants it accepted, the firmware should uppercase the root as the other verbs do).

behaviour: A verified OTA END restarts the board at once: locally 2 s after [OTA:END,OK], on a relay target 300 ms after its END ACK; both boot into the other slot at the same version with the same config.

?OTALOCAL,STATUS (also bare, trailing comma, any case) prints the chip family, firmware, running and next slot with addresses and sizes, and the session (idle / ACTIVE id=n x / y B); an unknown sub-command names the valid ones; ?OTALOCAL? and ?OTA? print help only.
gap: 'Next (OTA): none' (a partition table with no spare slot) is unreachable on min_spiffs.

behaviour: BEGIN,<size>,<family> supersedes any live session silently, refuses the other chip family (brick guard), size 0 or over the inactive slot, before any erase, with [OTA:BEGIN,ERR,0] and the session idle; an accepted BEGIN abandons a config pull job the board is sending, erases and prints 'BEGIN ok: session 1, N B → partition' with [OTA:BEGIN,OK,0]; a BEGIN usage error prints no marker.
gap: 'esp_ota_begin failed' (:136-139) and 'no inactive OTA partition' (:120-122) are unreachable on the bench.

behaviour: DATA,<offset>,<base64> writes only at the cursor: an accepted chunk ACKs [OTA:ACK,<cursor>], a duplicate or gap NAKs with the cursor and leaves the session, a chunk overrunning the declared size or failing esp_ota_write (no 0xE9 magic) aborts the session, base64 errors and chunks over 1024 B print no marker and keep the session, progress prints every 64 KB and at 100 %.

END refuses an incomplete image (ends the session, restores the baud), fails verify on a truncated or corrupted image or an image of the other chip declared as this family ('END verify FAILED ... current app intact', no reboot, no slot change), and on success sets the boot partition and reboots.
gap: 'END set_boot_partition failed' (:208-210) is unreachable.

behaviour: ABORT closes the session with no boot switch (silent when idle, always restores 115200); the 30 s idle reaper aborts a session no accepted chunk refreshed (a NAK does not refresh it locally); END/DATA/BAUD with no session print their exact lines.

?OTALOCAL,BAUD,<115200|230400|460800|921600|1000000> needs a live session, ACKs at the old rate then switches 20 ms later, is refused otherwise with [OTA:BAUD,ERR,115200]; the rate is restored to 115200 by ABORT, the idle timeout, END ERR, a rejected re-BEGIN, and by the reboot after END OK; BAUD does not refresh the idle window.
gap: Only 921600/460800 (whichever the host carries) and 115200 are ever switched to; 230400 and 1000000 are accepted by the parser but never exercised.
how: In ota.local_baud_invalid also bump to 230400 and 1000000 when the host link carries them (the _host_rate probe), run ?VERSION at each, then ABORT.

behaviour: ?OTA,<BEGIN|DATA|END|ABORT>,<target 1-20>,<session>,... builds the packet and unicasts it: a bad target, sub-command or DATA usage sends nothing; a DATA offset with a ':<crc32>' suffix is dropped on a CRC mismatch ('DROPPED: crc a != b', blaming a serial RX overflow within 2 s), the no-suffix warning prints once per boot, base64 errors (-42 chunk over 192 B, -44 junk) send nothing.
gap: The overflow-blame suffix ('— serial RX HAS OVERFLOWED, this is the cause') is only asserted absent; the positive case (a CRC mismatch within 2 s of a counted overflow) is untested.
how: Right after stats.usb_rx_overflow_line's overflow (serialRxOverflowLastMs fresh) send a mismatching ?OTA,DATA,2,s,0:DEADBEEF,AAAA within 2 s and assert the suffix on the DROPPED line.

behaviour: A relay frame or an ACK to a board not yet an ESP-NOW peer registers it on demand (otaEnsurePeer) so relay OTA works between boards never peered; a send that still fails prints '[OTA] <sub> -> WCB<n> send failed rc=... (ESP-NOW peer table full? cap 20)'.
gap: Every relay test targets W2 (a floor peer) or NaviCore (the registered special peer); the on-demand registration and the failure line are never exercised.
how: Lower W1's floor so W2 is not a peer (?WCBQ,1 with auto-join off and W2 forgotten), send ?OTA,BEGIN,2,<s>,4096,1 (refused by W2's brick guard, nothing erased) and expect [OTA:ACK,2,<s>,0,1] on W1; put ?WCBQ back. The failure line needs 20 registered peers (known-blocked class: WCB-WP59 ack_queue_and_peer_reregister).

behaviour: On the target a BEGIN/DATA/END/ABORT packet is accepted only with the mesh password and this board's number, run from loop() (queued off the receive callback), and ACKed [OTA:ACK] with the session's real state: BEGIN OK/ERR at 0, DATA OK with the cursor (a dup or gap re-ACKs, a wrong session gets ERR with the real cursor), the frame that tears the session down ERR, in-session frames keep the 30 s timeout alive, the timeout sends no ACK, END OK/ERR at 0, ABORT OK ignoring the id and killing a USB session too; END OK reboots 300 ms after the ACK.
gap: The addressed-to-another-board half of the gate needs a crafted packet (known: WCB-WP59 ota.packet_auth_gate); the 12-slot packet queue dropping when full is not observable.

behaviour: A relay prints the target's ACK as [OTA:ACK,<src>,<session>,<offset>,<status>] from loop() through the relay queue, only for ACKs carrying the password and addressed to it.
A relay BEGIN with family 0 to NaviCore (family 1) is refused by its brick guard before any erase and ACKed ERR; W1 relays a 4 KB session to NaviCore whose END fails verify.
Any ?OTALOCAL or ?OTA command pauses the RC-JSON telemetry relay for 8 s so ACK lines are not crowded out.
?OTALOCAL lines work over the WebSocket: a 4096-byte BEGIN, a 1024-byte DATA line ACKed [OTA:ACK,1024], ABORT leaves STATUS idle.
USB input lost to a full 8 KB RX ring is counted and ?STATS prints 'USB/S0 input: N RX overflow(s) - bytes were lost'; the console reader waits for queue room so a 700-command line still runs whole.

?WIFI,OFF saves OFF ('reboot to apply'); ?WIFI,AP,<ssid>,<pass> and ?WIFI,JOIN,<ssid>,<pass> (verb any case, the passphrase everything after the SSID: commas and a leading space kept, a trailing space trimmed by the line reader, a trailing '?' not the help trap) save for the next boot and confirm with the SSID (derived WCB-<alias|n> for an empty AP SSID) and the channel note; refused and unsaved: an AP password under 8 characters, JOIN with no name, an SSID over 32, an unknown verb.

?WIFI prints the block: Mode (OFF (ESP-NOW only) / AP / JOIN), AP SSID (with '(derived)') and 'AP password: set|NOT SET', Clients when up, Join SSID and 'Association: connected|not connected (N attempt(s))', Interface up|down, IP address, 'Radio channel : n  (mesh channel m)' with the OFF-MESH mismatch flag, the WS endpoint with its client count or NOT RUNNING, free heap and its minimum.
gap: 'AP password : NOT SET — AP will not start' (a saved pass under 8) and the '*** MISMATCH — OFF-MESH ***' suffix are unreachable through the setters.

behaviour: At boot in AP mode the SoftAP is raised in WIFI_AP_STA on the mesh channel (max 4 stations) before esp_now_init, the DHCP router option is cleared (clients get no gateway), '[WIFI] SoftAP "<ssid>" up on channel n — ws://192.168.4.1/ws' and the shared-channel line print; a saved password under 8 characters refuses to start an open AP; the mesh keeps delivering.
gap: The 4-station cap, the open-AP refusal at boot (unreachable: the setter refuses first), and the DHCP fault lines ('AP netif not ready', 'could not read the DHCP offer mask', 'DHCP server FAILED to restart') are not asserted.
how: The cap needs five stations (the PC, NaviCore's STA, two phones): attended only; the rest are fault paths.

behaviour: In JOIN mode the boot prints 'will join "<ssid>" on channel n'; each attempt scans the mesh channel alone for the SSID (never a band sweep) and WiFi.begin's with its BSSID, auto-reconnect off; 'still looking (attempt 1)' and every 12th; retries every 5 s for ever; 'joined ... after N attempt(s) — ws://.../ws' once an address is held; a lost association prints 'lost ... retrying every 5 s' and rejoins by itself; an AP that leaves the radio off the mesh channel is disconnected and the join settles for good; an association with no address for 20 s starts over.
gap: Not asserted: the off-mesh AP guard ('joined ... but its AP is on channel x, not y — that is OFF-MESH. Disconnecting.' then no retry), the 'associated ... but no address after 20 s — starting over' arm, and the boot line 'JOIN mode selected but no SSID is set' (unreachable through the setter).
how: Off-mesh arm (opt-in wifi_modes): move W2's AP off the mesh channel (?WCBCH on W2 + reboot: W2 is off the mesh meanwhile), JOIN W1 to it and assert the OFF-MESH line, Association 'not connected', the radio line still on the mesh channel, and no 'still looking' afterwards; put both back. The no-address arm needs an AP with DHCP off (none on the bench).

behaviour: Every 30 s while an interface is up the radio channel is compared with the mesh channel and a mismatch is reported ('WARNING: radio is on channel x but the mesh is on y').
gap: Nothing on the bench moves the radio off the channel while WiFi is up.
how: Only reachable with a fault knob (esp_wifi_set_channel from a ?DEBUG verb) or an AP that hops channels.

behaviour: The chain carries ?WIFI,AP,<ssid>,<pass> / ?WIFI,JOIN,... with the passphrase, or ?WIFI,OFF, so a restore brings the mode back; after an erase the token is ?WIFI,OFF and no SoftAP comes up.

The /ws endpoint starts on the first loop() pass with an interface up (AP or JOIN), prints '[WS] command endpoint ready — ws://<ip>/ws' (NaviLink's cue), is NOT RUNNING with WiFi off, and a failed start is not retried.
gap: The httpd/queue/URI start failures are fault paths.

behaviour: CR and LF both end a line and two lines in one frame both run; a line split over frames runs once; a leading space is trimmed; a line over 1535 characters is dropped whole (neither head nor tail runs, never a broadcast); a frame over 3072 bytes closes the socket and is counted in '[WS] dropped N inbound command(s)'.

Console output is teed to every client from a 2 KB sink flushed on the loop task, each text frame cut on a UTF-8 boundary; ?backup over the socket is whole and CRC-valid and ?HELP arrives line for line; overflow drops whole lines and reports '[WS] dropped N output line(s) — client too slow' from loop().
gap: The whole-line drop and its report (sinkDropping, :210-213; :448-449) are never produced: the sink only overflows off the loop task (a WiFi-task print burst) or faster than TCP drains.
how: With a client connected and not reading (a WsClient that never recv()s) run ?backup twice: once the TCP window is full the send fails and the session closes (#113); a tee drop needs a print burst from the receive callback, e.g. 30 mesh unicasts of ;S0<text> from W2 in one burst while the client is slow, then assert the '[WS] dropped' line on USB.

behaviour: At most two WebSocket clients (httpd max_open_sockets with LRU purge): a third evicts the least recently used, whose socket closes; each socket keeps its own line accumulator; a command typed over the socket resets the origin flags so a broadcast right after a mesh-received command still reaches the mesh.

A closed session releases its accumulator and sink slot and is closed with a reset (SO_LINGER 0); a failed send closes the session; when the AP's last station leaves every session from the AP subnet is closed at once, so a vanished client is dropped and its heap comes back.
Inbound lines go through a 6-deep queue, one run per loop() pass; the handler waits up to 50 ms for room and counts a refused line ('[WS] dropped N inbound command(s) — queue full or oversized').
gap: Only the oversized-frame count is asserted; a queue-full drop (more than 6 lines in one frame while loop() is held) is not.
how: Send one frame of 40 '?VERSION\n' lines while W1 prints ?backup (loop busy): expect fewer than 40 'End of Version' and a '[WS] dropped N inbound command(s)' line with N = 40 - answered.

behaviour: A WebSocket line takes the USB (source 0) path: ?VERSION answered over the socket, ;S0 markers come out on the console, W1 counts the client, and it leaves cleanly.
